Main article: [Suits season 2](/wiki/Suits_season_2 "Suits season 2")

Jessica learns Mike's secret, but other issues take precedence when the co-founding partner, Daniel Hardman, who left the firm in disgrace, returns in a power bid for control of the firm. Tensions rise as Jessica and Harvey find themselves opposed by Louis, who sides with Hardman after being promised a promotion to [senior partner](/wiki/Senior_partner "Senior partner"). Mike begins a romantic relationship with Rachel but wants to tell her the truth about his lack of qualifications. Harvey forbids him from doing this and so Mike breaks up with her. He pursues other women after his grandmother's sudden death. Harvey and Donna face accusations of burying evidence and must uncover the truth while keeping incriminating evidence from Hardman, who wants to use it to leverage a managing partner position. The increasing threat from Hardman forces Jessica into a [merger](/wiki/Mergers_and_acquisitions "Mergers and acquisitions") with a major British international law firm called Darby International, that is owned and managed by internationally renowned London corporate lawyer Edward Darby. Ultimately, Mike reveals his secret to Rachel.

Despite having lost in the playoffs, the team had very high expectations entering the [2020–21 season](/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_NHL_season "2020–21 NHL season"). The NHL did not begin the season until January 13, 2021, due to the ongoing global pandemic. NHL divisions would be temporarily realigned due to travel restrictions, placing the Flyers in the [East Division](/wiki/East_Division_(NHL) "East Division (NHL)").[[52]](#cite_note-55) The team managed to finish the first month of play tied for first place in the league, with a 7–2–1 record. However things began to unravel as the season continued. The team fell out of playoff contention by early March and would finish the season with the most goals scored against in the league. Management vowed to address the issues the team had suffered during the season by making several trades and free agent signings. On July 17, 2021, the team traded Nolan Patrick and [Philippe Myers](/wiki/Philippe_Myers "Philippe Myers") to the Nashville Predators in exchange for defenseman [Ryan Ellis](/wiki/Ryan_Ellis "Ryan Ellis").[[53]](#cite_note-56) The following week the team traded for defenseman [Rasmus Ristolainen](/wiki/Rasmus_Ristolainen "Rasmus Ristolainen") from the Buffalo Sabres in exchange for [Robert Hagg](/wiki/Robert_H%C3%A4gg "Robert Hägg"), a [2021](/wiki/2021_NHL_entry_draft "2021 NHL entry draft") first-round pick, and a [2023](/wiki/2023_NHL_entry_draft "2023 NHL entry draft") second-round pick; and traded Voracek back to the Columbus Blue Jackets for forward [Cam Atkinson](/wiki/Cam_Atkinson "Cam Atkinson").[[54]](#cite_note-57)[[55]](#cite_note-58) The team also signed veteran defenseman [Keith Yandle](/wiki/Keith_Yandle "Keith Yandle"), back up goaltender [Martin Jones](/wiki/Martin_Jones_(ice_hockey) "Martin Jones (ice hockey)") and forward [Derick Brassard](/wiki/Derick_Brassard "Derick Brassard") to short-term deals.[[56]](#ci

fanoutqa_021761.t: Saitama Seibu Lions :: Franchise history :: Nishitetsu Clippers (1950) :: chunk_0004
fanoutqa_021761.x:
Saitama Seibu Lions :: Franchise history :: Nishitetsu Clippers (1950) :: chunk_0004
In 1950, the team became a founding member of the [Pacific League](/wiki/Pacific_League "Pacific League"). It was then owned by a private railroad company [Nishi-Nippon Railroad](/wiki/Nishi-Nippon_Railroad "Nishi-Nippon Railroad"), well known as "Nishitetsu", which was based in [Fukuoka](/wiki/Fukuoka_Prefecture "Fukuoka Prefecture") in [Kyushu](/wiki/Kyushu "Kyushu"), the western area of Japan (Nishi-Nippon). The Clippers name was chosen as Nishitetsu was in charge of [Pan American Airlines](/wiki/Pan_Am "Pan Am")' Japanese operations (back then, Pan Am's jets were known as "Clippers" due to them being aeronautical [Boeing 314 Clipper](/wiki/Boeing_314_Clipper "Boeing 314 Clipper")).[[3]](#cite_note-5) The team finished sixth that year, and at the end of the season, Nishitetsu was merged with another professional baseball club in Fukuoka, the [Nishi-Nippon Pirates](/wiki/Nishi_Nippon_Pirates "Nishi Nippon Pirates"), which belonged to the [Central League](/wiki/Central_League "Central League") and managed by a local newspaper company the [Nishinippon Shimbun](/wiki/Nishinippon_Shimbun "Nishinippon Shimbun"). The new club was to form the **Nishitetsu Lions**. Thus the Lions name was adopted and has been retained up to today as the name of the franchise.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Flag_of_California_at_the_State_Capitol_in_September_2016.jpg/250px-Flag_of_California_at_the_State_Capitol_in_September_2016.jpg)](/wiki/File:Flag_of_California_at_the_State_Capitol_in_September_2016.jpg)

The flag on display at the [California State Capitol](/wiki/California_State_Capitol "California State Capitol").

The first official version of the Bear Flag was adopted by the [California State Legislature](/wiki/California_State_Legislature "California State Legislature") and signed into law by [Governor](/wiki/Governor_of_California "Governor of California") [Hiram Johnson](/wiki/Hiram_Johnson "Hiram Johnson") in 1911 as the official state flag.[[9]](#cite_note-csl-9-6-9)

The contemporary state flag is white with a wide red strip along the bottom. There is a red star in the upper left corner and a [California grizzly bear](/wiki/California_grizzly_bear "California grizzly bear") facing left (toward the hoist) in the center, walking on a patch of green grass. The size of the bear is two-thirds the size of the hoist width and has a ratio of 2 by 1. The grass plot has a ratio of 11 to 1.[[2]](#cite_note-csl-h-c-2) The five-point star is taken from the California Lone Star Flag of 1836.[[6]](#cite_note-caguard-6) The hoist of the flag is two-thirds the fly.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

The bear on one 1911 version of the flag is claimed to have been modeled on the last [California grizzly bear](/wiki/California_golden_bear "California golden bear") in captivity.[[11]](#cite_note-11) The bear, named "[Monarch](/wiki/Monarch_(bear) "Monarch (bear)")", was captured in 1889 by newspaper reporter Allan Kelly, at the behest of [William Randolph Hearst](/wiki/William_Randolph_Hearst "William Randolph Hearst").[[12]](#cite_note-12) The bear was subsequently moved to [Woodwards Gardens](/wiki/Woodward%27s_Gardens "Woodward's Gardens") in San Francisco, and then to

Hou and Ko both support gradually increasing the use of nuclear energy, (Hou supported 18% use by 2050) while the DPP's Lai supports eliminating nuclear energy by 2050. All three candidates agreed to increase use of renewables.[[70]](#cite_note-70) The KMT vice presidential nominee criticized the use of solar energy, preferring nuclear power instead.[[71]](#cite_note-auto5-71) Cost of living featured as a topic of debate, with a third of voters saying economic issues were pressing. Both Lai and Hou pledged to increase the minimum wage.[[72]](#cite_note-auto2-72) Lai acknowledged there were shortcomings in the government's approach to help younger people in the country, promising minimum wage would increase from NT$26,400 to NT$27,470 by 2025.[[73]](#cite_note-73) Additionally, Lai vowed to offer financial support to Taiwanese start-up companies, saying he would allocate NT$150 billion for small business investment.[[74]](#cite_note-74) Ko offered plans to integrate hospitals and bolster the medical field, while the KMT's Hou promised to address mental health.[[71]](#cite_note-auto5-71)

Nouvelle-Aquitaine :: Geography :: chunk_0003
At 84,061 square kilometres, Nouvelle-Aquitaine is larger than [French Guiana](/wiki/French_Guiana "French Guiana"), which makes it the largest region of [metropolitan](/wiki/Metropolitan_France "Metropolitan France") and [overseas France](/wiki/Overseas_France "Overseas France").

Nouvelle-Aquitaine is delimited by four other French regions ([Pays de la Loire](/wiki/Pays_de_la_Loire "Pays de la Loire") to the north-west, [Centre-Val de Loire](/wiki/Centre-Val_de_Loire "Centre-Val de Loire") to the northeast, [Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes](/wiki/Auvergne-Rh%C3%B4ne-Alpes "Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes") to the east, and [Occitania](/wiki/Occitania_(administrative_region) "Occitania (administrative region)") to the south-east), three autonomous communities in [Spain](/wiki/Spain "Spain") to the south (from east to west, [Aragon](/wiki/Aragon "Aragon"), [Navarre](/wiki/Navarre "Navarre"), and [Basque Country](/wiki/Basque_Country_(autonomous_community) "Basque Country (autonomous community)")), and the North [Atlantic Ocean](/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") (the eastern part of [Bay of Biscay](/wiki/Bay_of_Biscay "Bay of Biscay"), *Golfe de Gascogne* in French) to the west.

Nouvelle-Aquitaine comprises twelve [departments](/wiki/Departments_of_France "Departments of France"): [Charente](/wiki/Charente "Charente"), [Charente-Maritime](/wiki/Charente-Maritime "Charente-Maritime"), [Corrèze](/wiki/Corr%C3%A8ze "Corrèze"), [Creuse](/wiki/Creuse "Creuse"), [Dordogne](/wiki/Dordogne "Dordogne"), [Gironde](/wiki/Gironde "Gironde"), [Landes](/wiki/Landes_(department) "Landes (department)"), [Lot-et-Garonne](/wiki/Lot-et-Garonne "Lot-et-Garonne"), [Pyrénées-Atlantiques](/wiki/Pyr%C3%A9n%C3%A9es-Atlantiques "Pyrénées-Atlantiques"), [Deux-Sèvres](/wiki/Deux-S%C3%A8vres "Deux-Sèvres"), [Vienne](/wiki/Vienne_(department) "Vienne (department)") and [Haute-Vienne](/wiki/Haute-Vienne "Haute-Vienne").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/TGDModelSpillwayView.jpg/250px-TGDModelSpillwayView.jpg)](/wiki/File:TGDModelSpillwayView.jpg)

Model of the Three Gorges Dam looking upstream, showing the dam body (middle left), the spillway (middle of the dam body) and the ship lift (to the right).

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/TGDModelShipLocks.jpg/250px-TGDModelShipLocks.jpg)](/wiki/File:TGDModelShipLocks.jpg)

Model of the Three Gorges Dam showing the ship lift and the ship lock. The ship lift is to the right of the dam body with its own designated waterway. The ship locks are to the right (northeast) of the ship lift.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/TGDModelAuxSouthDam.jpg/250px-TGDModelAuxSouthDam.jpg)](/wiki/File:TGDModelAuxSouthDam.jpg)

Earthfill south dam in foreground with view along main dam. The wall beyond is to separate spillway and turbine flows from the lock and ship lift upstream approach channel. A similar separation is used on the downstream side, seen partially in the preceding image.

Made of concrete and steel, the dam is 2,335 m (2,554 yd; 1.451 mi) long and 185 m (607 ft) above sea level at its top. The project used 27.2 million m3 (35.6 million yd3) of concrete (mainly for the dam wall), used 463,000 [tonnes](/wiki/Tonne "Tonne") of steel (enough to build 63 [Eiffel Towers](/wiki/Eiffel_Tower "Eiffel Tower")), and moved about 102.6 million m3 (134.2 million yd3) of earth.[[44]](#cite_note-ibib1-46) The concrete dam wall is 181 m (594 ft) high above the rock basis.

When the water level is at its maximum of 175 m (574 ft) above sea level, 110 m (361 ft) higher than the river level downstream, the dam reservoir is on average about 660 km (410 mi) in length and 1.12 km (3,675 ft) in width. It contains 39.3 km3 (31,900,000 [acre⋅ft](/wiki/Acre-foot "Acre-foot")) of water and has a total surface area of 1,045 km2 (403 sq mi)

In May 1962, Soviet First Secretary [Nikita Khrushchev](/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev "Nikita Khrushchev") decided to counter the growing lead of the US in developing and deploying strategic missiles by placing Soviet intermediate-range nuclear missiles in Cuba, despite the misgivings of the Soviet Ambassador in Havana, [Alexandr Ivanovich Alexeyev](/wiki/Alexander_Alexeyev_(diplomat) "Alexander Alexeyev (diplomat)"), who argued that Castro would not accept them.[[38]](#cite_note-38) Khrushchev faced a strategic situation in which the US was perceived to have a "splendid [first strike](/wiki/Pre-emptive_nuclear_strike "Pre-emptive nuclear strike")" capability that put the Soviet Union at a disadvantage. In 1962, the Soviets had only 20 [ICBMs](/wiki/ICBM "ICBM") capable of delivering nuclear warheads to the US from inside the Soviet Union.[[39]](#cite_note-Allison_1999_92-39) Their poor accuracy and reliability raised serious doubts about their effectiveness. A newer, more reliable generation of [Soviet ICBMs](/wiki/Soviet_missile_program "Soviet missile program") only became operational after 1965.[[39]](#cite_note-Allison_1999_92-39)

Soviet nuclear capability in 1962 placed less emphasis on ICBMs than on medium and intermediate-range ballistic missiles ([MRBMs](/wiki/Medium-range_ballistic_missile "Medium-range ballistic missile") and [IRBMs](/wiki/Intermediate-range_ballistic_missile "Intermediate-range ballistic missile")) which could strike American allies and most of [Alaska](/wiki/Alaska "Alaska") from Soviet territory, but not the [contiguous United States](/wiki/Contiguous_United_States "Contiguous United States"). Breast cancer :: Health disparities in breast cancer :: chunk_0028
There are ethnic disparities in the [mortality rates](/wiki/Mortality_rate "Mortality rate") for breast cancer as well as in breast cancer treatment. Breast cancer is the most prevalent cancer affecting women of every ethnic group in the United States. Breast cancer incidence among Black women aged 45 and older is higher than that of white women in the same age group. White women aged 60–84 have higher incidence rates of breast cancer than Black women. Despite this, Black women at every age are more likely to die of breast cancer.[[187]](#cite_note-Health_and_Racial_Disparity_in_Brea-187)

Breast cancer treatment has improved greatly over the years; however, Black women are still less likely to obtain treatment compared to white women.[[187]](#cite_note-Health_and_Racial_Disparity_in_Brea-187) Risk factors such as [socioeconomic status](/wiki/Socioeconomic_status "Socioeconomic status"), late-stage, or breast cancer at diagnosis, genetic differences in tumor subtypes, and differences in healthcare access all contribute to these disparities. Socioeconomic determinants affecting the disparity in breast cancer illness include poverty, [culture](/wiki/Cultural_differences_in_breast_cancer_diagnosis_and_treatment "Cultural differences in breast cancer diagnosis and treatment"), and social injustice. In Hispanic women, the incidence of breast cancer is lower than in non-Hispanic women, but it is often diagnosed at a later stage than in white women with larger tumors.

Black women are usually diagnosed with breast cancer at a younger age than white women. The median age of diagnosis for Black women is 59, in comparison to 62 in White women. The incidence of breast cancer in Black women has increased by 0.4% per year since 1975, and 1.5% per year among Asian/Pacific Islander women since 1992. Ryan Fitzpatrick :: Professional career :: Tennessee Titans :: chunk_0010
On March 18, 2013, Fitzpatrick signed a two-year contract with the [Tennessee Titans](/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans").[[54]](#cite_note-54)

During a Week 4 38–13 victory over the [New York Jets](/wiki/2013_New_York_Jets_season "2013 New York Jets season"), Fitzpatrick made his Titans debut, replacing an injured [Jake Locker](/wiki/Jake_Locker "Jake Locker") in the third quarter. Fitzpatrick completed three of eight passes for 108 yards and a 77-yard touchdown pass to [Nate Washington](/wiki/Nate_Washington "Nate Washington").[[55]](#cite_note-55)

Fitzpatrick played in 11 games and started in nine of them. He finished the season with a 3–6 record as the starting quarterback, beating division rivals [Jacksonville Jaguars](/wiki/2013_Jacksonville_Jaguars_season "2013 Jacksonville Jaguars season") and [Houston Texans](/wiki/2013_Houston_Texans_season "2013 Houston Texans season") in the final two games of the season. Fitzpatrick completed the season throwing for 2,454 yards, 14 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions to go along with 43 carries for 225 yards and three touchdowns.[[56]](#cite_note-56)

Fitzpatrick was released on March 14, 2014, and replaced by [Charlie Whitehurst](/wiki/Charlie_Whitehurst "Charlie Whitehurst").[[57]](#cite_note-57)
